steps.why: The half swing is the useful unit: that is what a clock counts to make one tick.
common_mistakes: Saying its time period is 1 second — 1 second is the half swing, not the full period.

recall.must_convey: That a seconds pendulum has a time period of 2 seconds, so each half swing takes 1 second.

steps.memory_tip: The word seconds refers to the tick, not the full period: one second per tick, two seconds per period.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two seconds for the full period, said in words.

steps.label: The length
lines: Since g changes from place to place, this
length is not exactly the same everywhere.
steps.why: The arithmetic gives L = 39.2/39.48 ≈ 0.99 m; the book rounds this to 1 metre. Quote 0.99 m when a numerical value is asked. The length depends on g, so it differs slightly from place to place.
common_mistakes: Quoting 1 metre as an exact universal value.

recall.must_convey: That the length works out to about 1 metre from T equals 2 pi root L by g.
accept: L is g T squared by four pi squared

steps.memory_tip: 4π² ≈ 39.5 and gT² = 9.8 × 4 = 39.2. The two nearly cancel, which is why L is near 1 m.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show T = 2 s going into T = 2π√(L/g) before writing the length.

insider_note: The length is a separate mark, so finish the arithmetic — quote 0.99 m, or 1 metre stated as a rounded value.
